scope: Deterministic per-tenant audit-chain topology, canonical version-2 event hashing, legacy graph preflight, and fail-closed database constraints

defect.failureMode: A late event with an older business instant, or equal-time events ordered by unrelated random UUIDs, could leave an already-consumed predecessor eligible for reuse and fork a tenant chain.

implementedControls: business occurred_at remains evidence/display chronology and no longer defines chain order
writer holds the tenant advisory transaction lock and selects the sole event with no child as the topological head
zero heads with existing rows or more than one head raises AuditChainIntegrityError before insert
repository-authored rows explicitly use hash version 2
version-2 SHA-256 input binds tenant, event ID, actor, action, resource, correlation, reason, before/after values, version context, normalized UTC time, predecessor, and hash-version domain
canonical JSON recursively sorts object keys while preserving array order and explicit nulls
migration 0039 labels preserved existing rows as version 1 without recomputing or rewriting evidence
migration preflight aborts on malformed or duplicate hashes, forked predecessors, self-references, missing or multiple genesis events, orphans, unreachable events, and disconnected cycles
tenant-scoped unique event-hash and predecessor-hash indexes enforce one digest and one child
partial tenant genesis uniqueness permits exactly one null predecessor after the first insert
tenant-composite self-foreign key prevents orphaned and cross-tenant predecessor references
same-lock BEFORE INSERT validation requires every non-replay row to create genesis or extend the current head and blocks disconnected multi-row cycles
hash-format, self-reference, and bounded hash-version checks fail closed
existing append-only trigger and update/delete/truncate role denial remain in force
runbook classifies topology or migration-preflight failure as an integrity incident and forbids silent re-chaining

checks: production builds across all applicable workspace projects, including Next.js

covered: equivalent timezone instants produce the same digest
nested object key order does not change the digest
tenant, reason, after-value, and predecessor mutations change the digest
malformed predecessor and invalid instant fail closed
migration text requires every legacy preflight and topology constraint

browserRegression.interpretation: No operator regression was introduced; audit topology has no new browser surface.

missingConfiguration: DATABASE_ADMIN_URL and related PostgreSQL role URLs
plannedAuditCoverage: apply migration 0039 through the least-privilege migration role
append an old-business-time event and an equal-time successor to the actual topological head
serialize two concurrent application-role writers into one chain and retain exactly one head
reject a direct second child, orphan, second genesis, self-reference, and cross-tenant predecessor
reject a disconnected two-event cycle supplied in one multi-row insert
exercise the preflight against valid and intentionally corrupt populated previous-release databases
liveIntegrationAttempt.interpretation: No integration assertion ran. The three new PostgreSQL test cases and migration execution remain unavailable evidence, not passing results.

operationalImpact.rollback: Leave migration 0039 and immutable rows in place. Stop audit-producing mutations and restore the compatible writer or ship an approved forward repair; do not drop constraints or restore the business-time writer while writes continue.

remainingEvidenceAndOperationalRisks: Run migration 0039 from empty and a populated previous supported release through the migration, application, and worker roles.
Measure repeated preflight scans, transactional unique-index builds, lock waits, and disk impact at representative audit volume with reviewed lock and statement timeouts.
Exercise application-role late/equal-time and concurrent writers plus every direct database constraint negative.
Restore an isolated backup and verify full per-tenant genesis reachability, one head, and version-2 recomputation.
Design and review external integrity anchoring, key custody, availability, privacy, and disaster recovery if independent notarization is required.
Version-1 hashes are preserved historical evidence but arbitrary legacy JavaScript object insertion order may not be portably recomputable.
A fully compromised database owner or host is outside the protection of database-local hash chaining and append-only triggers.
No production, staging, hosted CI, backup/restore, representative-volume, or external-anchor result is claimed.
